headline: High-risk default interaction: nullclaw can read/write and use network/MCP while dagster is a non-runnable orchestrator, creating leakage, conflict, and cascading-error paths if paired in a shared workspace.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Dagster has no filesystem or clipboard surfaces, so it cannot directly ingest Nullclaw output by default. However, Nullclaw can read/write files, use stdin/stdout, browser, and MCP, so if Dagster artifacts are placed in the shared workspace, Nullclaw content could be treated as trusted instructions. The pathway is plausible but not default for Dagster alone.
conditions: IF Dagster artifacts are copied into ~/.nullclaw/workspace/ and then parsed as instructions by Nullclaw
IF a shared file or MCP channel is introduced between the agents
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate workspaces
Disable file-based instruction parsing in Nullclaw
Use read-only exports from Dagster
Add provenance labels to any shared artifacts
requires-engineering: enforce channel allowlists

B_data_leakage.rationale: Dagster is documented as not reading or writing the filesystem and touching no data classes, while Nullclaw explicitly reads/writes workspace files and handles secrets, logs, memory, and agent metadata. If Dagster outputs are exported into Nullclaw's workspace, sensitive operational data can flow into a broader-IO agent. The pairwise leakage path exists through shared files, though Dagster itself is low-exposure.
conditions: IF Dagster outputs are written into ~/.nullclaw/workspace/
IF those files contain secrets, tokens, or audit data
mitigations: Do not place secrets in shared files
Mount separate workspaces per agent
Redact sensitive fields before transfer
Review Nullclaw retention/logging settings
requires-engineering: add DLP controls

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Dagster has no write, git, shell, or network capabilities in the profile, so it cannot contend for mutable resources. Nullclaw can write files, modify git state, and use broad network, but without Dagster write surfaces there is no meaningful write-write conflict. Any conflict would require unusual external orchestration not shown in the profiles.
conditions: IF an external orchestrator grants Dagster write or git permissions not shown in its profile
IF both agents are pointed at the same mutable directory
mitigations: Keep Dagster read-only
Avoid shared git worktrees
Serialize any file updates through one agent
Use per-agent directories
requires-engineering: add locking around shared state

D_cascading_error.rationale: Dagster is an orchestrator, so its outputs may be consumed downstream, while Nullclaw can act on files, webhooks, and scheduled tasks. If Dagster-produced artifacts are fed into Nullclaw without verification, Nullclaw may execute or relay incorrect pipeline facts. The pairwise cascade is plausible in default integration patterns, though not proven by direct evidence.
conditions: IF Nullclaw consumes Dagster-generated artifacts as authoritative input
IF no validation step checks Dagster outputs before Nullclaw acts
mitigations: Insert a validation step between agents
Require schema checks on Dagster outputs
Mark Dagster outputs as untrusted by default
Limit Nullclaw actions to dry-run mode
requires-engineering: add approval gates for downstream actions

E_compliance.rationale: Dagster is open-source and shows no touched data classes, while Nullclaw explicitly handles secrets, workspace files, audit logs, and agent metadata. If regulated data is routed from Dagster into Nullclaw's broader logging and workspace surfaces, retention or residency mismatches can arise. Dagster is not cited for a specific compliance regime, so the risk is inferred from Nullclaw's documented data handling.
conditions: IF regulated data from Dagster is stored in Nullclaw workspace files or audit logs
IF retention or deletion requirements apply to those records
mitigations: Avoid routing regulated data into Nullclaw logs
Set short retention on workspace artifacts
Pseudonymize records before transfer
Document data-handling boundaries
requires-engineering: implement residency and retention controls
